ogTitle: Help Us Save Talking Horse Ranch — Camas Commons Land Trust
ogDescription: Pledge or donate today to help preserve 40 acres of San Juan Island farmland for perpetually affordable leases & community resilience.

sections.welcomeText: Welcome to a new model for farming. We are Ally and Guisepi, two land stewards & community enthusiasts committed to continuing on our little island’s tradition of small-scale, regenerative farming for future generations… This is Camas Commons.

sections.title: What is Camas Commons?
sections.content: Based at Talking Horse Ranch Camas Commons is a nonprofit regenerative farming land trust being created to provide perpetually affordable residential and agricultural leases to farmers and producers on San Juan Island, WA. In a time when talented young makers and producers are priced out of life on San Juan. Camas Commons provides land accessibility and affordable housing for young farmers regenerates the land and supports the local community with healthy food and community events.

sections.title: How can I support this project?
sections.content:
Our proposal to acquire Talking Horse Ranch is due in September and the time to secure its future is now. We are ready to continue stewarding this land as a working farm, a place of conservation and a lasting community resource. But we cannot do it without significant financial support. We are seeking lead donors prepared to make transformational gifts toward the purchase of the ranch. Your support can help protect this land from speculation keep it affordable for future farmers and producers and preserve it in service to the community for generations to come. 

Our first major fundraising deadline is in mid-September, when we submit our final proposal to the Land Bank. To make that proposal competitive, we need to raise $1.5 million.
It is an ambitious goal, but the opportunity is extraordinary: to secure the future of Talking Horse Ranch as protected farmland and a lasting community resource. Every contribution brings us closer—and every donor becomes part of preserving this land for generations to come.

sections.title: Why Supporting Our Land Trust Matters…
sections.content: We believe this land is meant to be shared, and with us stewarding it, you can guarantee this legacy we’ve begun will continue. This project aims to help alleviate many of the issues facing our community, like young people leaving the island, farmers aging-out, skyrocketing land and housing costs, supply chain issues, and more. Creating this land trust will help maintain a web of resilience in our local community though food sovereignty, land connection, and attracting and keeping talented makers and growers on our island.

sections.title: FAQ:

items.q: What is this land all about?
items.a:
This 120-acre farm has seen a lot — a historic dairy, an eccentric follower of the spiritual leader Ramtha, a golf course, and an organic farm. For the past 20 years, this farm has been known as Talking Horse Ranch, after the famed “talking horse” purchased by previous owner Ernie Kanzler Jr. from the channeler of his spiritual guru, Ramtha.

For these past 20-years the farm has been under-managed, and kept running at a low-idle. Most of the infrastructure is in disrepair, but not beyond the point-of-no-return.

Despite all this, the land is a wonderfully magical place — with excellent topography, landscape, a seasonal creek, 6 ponds, enchanting forests, and incredibly cool and quirky buildings and landscaping. Most of the developed land is south facing slope with excellent sun, the wells produce an incredible 45 and 70 GPM, and the big barn offers 13,000 square feet of usable indoor space. These are just a few of the significant attributes.

40 of the 120 acres will be purchased for Camas Commons, with the other 80 acres entering into perpetual conservation through the San Juan Conservation Land Bank. Together, public access will be included in this plan with a walking trail that connects the Beaverton Marsh Preserve to the top of Beaver Hill, through Camas Commons.

Residential Members will have the option to own their own home and sign a 99-year lease, or lease a home from the land trust. They, and Non-Residential Members, will have the opportunity to lease land, infrastructure, or buildings with short-term leases for agricultural, traditional craft, forestry, or other sustainability-related endeavors.

items.q: How many people will live at Camas Commons?
items.a: Based on the allowed density, four houses plus the existing ADU are permissible. Averaging 2-3 people per house, we see 10-15 full time residents. At least one member from each house must be involved in agriculture, sustainability-adjacent activities, or an administrative role.

items.q: What will this project offer the local community?
items.a: Members of Camas Commons will be producing agricultural products, like fruits, vegetables, eggs and more, as well as useful and traditional crafts and land-connection events. There may also be educational workshops, seasonal gatherings, petting zoos, live music, a farm store and more.

items.q: How can I get a lease at Camas Commons?
items.a: Applications for residential leases will open within a year of the purchase of the land. Agricultural leases may open sooner than that. If you want to be on a list, please contact us at info@camascommons.org

Current Talking Horse Ranch land stewards Guisepi Spadafora and Ally Rugge have been helping facilitate a path towards this goal for the past several years. Guisepi grew up on the island, and after years of service-based travel (i.e. the Free Tea Bus [freeteaparty.org](https://freeteaparty.org)), returned to the islands with his now wife, Ally, to find the right piece of land to dedicate themselves to. He has 20 years of experience in the nonprofit world, and loves to tinker. Ally has lived and worked on Talking Horse Ranch three times in the past 15 years, learning to grow food, rehabilitate soil, and raise chickens and dairy goats ([women-who-stare-at-goats-collective](https://www.visitsanjuans.com/account/women-who-stare-at-goats-collective)). They got married on the farm in 2023.

items.q: How can I support Camas Commons?
items.a: Please consider pledging or donating money to our cause. All pledges will only be collected if our proposal is chosen and we make our fundraising goals.
